issues.description: Unreachable `break` after `raise` and misuse of PerformanceWarning as an exception
issues.detail: The `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` is immediately followed by `break`, which is dead code — control never reaches it. More fundamentally, PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass being raised as an exception; the function name and test (`pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning)`) conflate `warnings.warn` semantics with `raise`. Pick one contract and state it in the docstring.

issues.description: Asymptotically-wrong `safe_chunk_size` formula multiplies all axes together
issues.detail: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` computes the byte size of a full N-dimensional shard, but the loop is per-axis and the divisibility failure is per-axis. For a 3D array with shard (12,12,12) and 8-byte dtype the message recommends 13824 bytes when a single axis misalignment may need far less. The arithmetic doesn't survive audit; state and verify the invariant `chunk_bytes >= prod(shard_shape) * itemsize` explicitly.

issues.description: Loop invariant for the divisibility check is never stated and only inspects `dw[0]`
issues.detail: The check reads `dw[0]` as the "nominal" dask chunk size, but `normalize_chunks` can return heterogeneous tuples (e.g. last chunk is the remainder). The implicit invariant — "every interior chunk along axis ax is a multiple of zw" — is neither written down nor verified. A literate comment naming the invariant and a check over all-but-last entries would make the intent provable rather than tried.

Due to Python precedence this parses as `not ((x % zw) == 0)`, which happens to be correct, but it forces the reader to re-derive the precedence rules. Write `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:` — the reader is the constraint, and this is library code that will outlive its author.

issues.description: Test asserts `pytest.raises` on a class named `PerformanceWarning` — contract confusion leaks into tests
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` is named "warns" but uses `pytest.raises`, not `pytest.warns`. Either the production code should `warnings.warn(...)` and the test use `pytest.warns`, or the class should be renamed (e.g. `ShardAlignmentError`) and the test renamed accordingly. The current pairing teaches future maintainers the wrong mental model.

issues.description: Open design question in PR description is not resolved in code or comment
issues.detail: The author asks whether an exception is appropriate when global `array.chunk-size` competes with shard shape; the diff silently chooses "raise" without recording the decision near the raise site. A short literate comment stating the policy ("global config wins for safety; we refuse rather than silently misalign") would make the next maintainer's job tractable.

review.summary: The change is directionally right — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` to let `auto_chunks` pick a shard-aligned multiple is a sound data-structure-first move. But the safety net has two audit failures: the `raise` is followed by an unreachable `break`, and the recommended `safe_chunk_size` multiplies all shard dimensions together while the divisibility check is per-axis, so the suggested config value is asymptotically wrong for N>1. The loop invariant ("every interior dask chunk along each axis is a multiple of the shard length along that axis") is never stated, and the code inspects only `dw[0]` as if it were representative. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED, with one ASYMPTOTICALLY-WRONG arithmetic bug in the user-facing remediation message. Fix the invariant and the bytes formula, decide between raise-vs-warn, and add one literate comment block; the rest is fine.
